public_rationale: A primary clinical study documents GPT-4 antibiotic recommendations that expert reviewers classified as harmful against clinical standards. That satisfies the ordinary meaning of some very bad advice. Other recommendations were optimal, which does not contradict this limited existential claim.
limitations: The study concerns a particular infectious-disease setting and does not measure all GPT-4 advice.
Potential harm was assessed; actual patient injury was not established.
The readable primary record is the study abstract, not the complete case-level dataset.
The event is dated only to 2023; the availability date conservatively uses the record's 2024 issue date.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Some of GPT-4's advice will be very bad.

statement.excerpt: Some of its advice will be head-scratchingly bad.
statement.document_title: What to Expect When You’re Expecting … GPT-4

our_interpretation: The target is advice generated by released GPT-4.
The plain reading is that at least some recommendations will be substantively and seriously wrong or potentially harmful under established factual or safety standards.
The phrase does not require showing that most advice is bad or that someone acted on it.
criteria.support_condition: A documented GPT-4 recommendation is assessed as seriously erroneous or potentially harmful against established standards by qualified evaluators.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A decisive demonstration rules out qualifying bad advice within the claimed scope. A finite sample of good advice alone cannot refute this unrestricted existential forecast.

evidence.publisher: Clinical Infectious Diseases; abstract hosted by PubMed
evidence.explanation: Two infectious-disease physicians assessed GPT-4 management recommendations against clinical literature and guidelines and identified harmful antibiotic advice. The same evaluation found optimal antibiotic recommendations in other cases, so it supports some bad advice without establishing universal failure.

conclusive_event.meets_rule: The study documents instances of GPT-4 advice independently assessed as harmful, satisfying the existential prediction.
